system.name: ZooRoute
system.one_liner: a cloud network reliability system that reroutes traffic around failures by varying the VXLAN outer source port to steer ECMP hashing onto pre-probed candidate paths

components.name: Outer MAC/IP/UDP Header
components.role: outer transport header added by the VTEP for VXLAN encapsulation

components.name: VXLAN Header
components.role: VXLAN tunnel header identifying the tenant's virtual network

components.name: Inner MAC/IP Header
components.role: original tenant packet header preserved inside the tunnel

components.name: srcIP
components.role: outer source IP, part of the 5-tuple the underlay ECMP-hashes on

components.name: srcPort
components.role: outer source port; undefined by the VXLAN standard and freely rewritten by ZooRoute to steer ECMP path selection

components.name: dstIP
components.role: outer destination IP, set to the destination VM's host

components.name: dstPort
components.role: outer destination port, fixed to 4789 per the VXLAN standard

components.name: protocol
components.role: outer transport protocol field of the 5-tuple

components.name: Tenant application
components.role: source of the original packet before VTEP encapsulation

components.name: Overlay
components.role: CSP-owned layer where ZooRoute rewrites the outer source port

components.name: ZooRoute
components.role: modifies the outer source port at the VTEP to trigger path switching, transparent to tenants

components.name: Physical network
components.role: underlay that performs ECMP hashing on the outer 5-tuple, oblivious to inner headers

components.name: Src
components.role: source endpoint of the probed candidate paths

components.name: Dst
components.role: destination endpoint of the probed candidate paths

components.name: Candidate paths via srcPort probing
components.role: labels the set of alternate paths ZooRoute proactively probes, each mapped to a source port

content.key_idea: ZooRoute reroutes traffic around failures by rewriting only the otherwise-undefined outer source port of the VXLAN header at the overlay VTEP, which changes ECMP hashing in the underlay and switches traffic onto a different, pre-probed candidate path.
content.reading_order: Top: packet header zoomed into its outer 5-tuple. Bottom-left: Tenant application through Overlay (ZooRoute) to Physical network. Bottom-right: Src-to-Dst mesh contrasting a failed path with a working backup.

encoding.emphasis: the red X on the orange srcPort:17 path versus the unbroken green srcPort:24 path is the figure's punchline: changing only the outer source port reroutes traffic around a failure

summary: This figure conveys ZooRoute's key idea: rerouting traffic by rewriting one field of the packet's outer header. At top, a packet is broken into Outer MAC/IP/UDP Header, VXLAN Header, Inner MAC/IP Header, and Payload, then zoomed into the outer 5-tuple (srcIP, srcPort, dstIP, dstPort, protocol), highlighting srcPort as the field ZooRoute controls. At bottom-left, a Tenant application's packet passes through the Overlay layer, where ZooRoute rewrites the outer source port, before reaching the Physical network, which performs ECMP hashing only on this outer 5-tuple. At bottom-right, an abstract Src-to-Dst mesh shows two example paths keyed by source port: srcPort:17 fails partway (red X), so traffic switches to the pre-probed, working srcPort:24 backup path -- illustrating ZooRoute's candidate-path probing and deterministic recovery.
